title: Correctness of compiled conditions
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, let $Z$ be a compiler size record with local-variable bound $F$ and stack bound $Q$, and let $[1m\sigma[0m$ be a program state represented by a word-RAM memory $m$ in a frame at stack position $q$. Suppose the frame representation stores the designated words $1$, $0$, and $-1$ at their respective addresses, stores each pool index $n$ up to the dispatcher position at its pool address, stores the frame pointer at the stack address for $q$, and stores each local value and memory value at the corresponding stack address and memory address within their specified bounds; also suppose $1\le q$, $q+F\le Q$, and every value of the state has absolute value at most the word bound. If a condition $c$ has width at most $F$, is safe for the resource limits and state, and its compiled code occurs at position $pos$ in a program, then there are a memory $m'$ and a number $n\le\mathrm{size}(c)$ such that $m'$ agrees with $m$ outside the scratch and temporary addresses for $F$ local variables. Execution from $pos$ reaches $pos+\mathrm{size}(c)$ in $n$ steps when $c$ holds, and reaches the specified target position $l$ in $n$ steps when $c$ does not hold, with the same resulting memory $m'$.
hypotheses_covered: A size record with word width W, local-variable bound F, and stack bound Q
A state and memory satisfying the framed representation
Frame bounds 1 ≤ q and q + F ≤ Q
All state location and memory values have absolute value at most the word bound
Compiled condition code occurs at position pos
Condition width is at most F
Condition is safe for the limits and state
